conditions: §R1a — every call is cost-ledgered with the ledger committed as evidence; an unledgered call is a defect

§R1b — the budget is per-sprint and does NOT roll over; at exhaustion the harness records BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and continues offline, and never silently degrades to fixtures while still labelling output as live
§R1c — the deterministic offline path stays REQUIRED; the live budget exists to prove the live path works, not to replace the fixture path

§R1d — the budget authorizes EXECUTION only. It does not authorize a review to approve anything: 'Claude must not self-approve any gate' and 'the OWNER remains final authority' stay binding, and a live finding is evidence feeding the fail-closed gate, never a verdict
ledger_of_record: THIS FILE. cost_ledger.ApiCallRecord is keyed to a pipeline Task and record_claude() is a documented no-op without one; a roadmap-level visual review has no Task, so the committed per-call entries below are the ledger §R1a requires. Costs are computed with the same cost_ledger.claude_cost_usd pricing table used for task-attached calls.

calls.DEFECT: THIS CALL WAS SPENT AND IS NOT PROPERLY LEDGERED. The first live invocation reached the provider and returned a response, but the command parsed the JSON payload BEFORE writing the ledger entry, and the parse raised (the reply was truncated at max_tokens=4096 mid-JSON), so the response object — and with it the request id, token counts and cost — was lost before it was recorded. §R1a calls an unledgered call a defect; this entry records the defect rather than hiding the spend. The counted spend is therefore CORRECT (one call consumed, 9 remaining) while this row's identity fields are honestly UNKNOWN and can never be recovered. Fixed forward: the ledger write now happens immediately after the call returns and before any parsing, and max_tokens was raised to 16000. Recorded against class 'derived quantity published without recoverable inputs' — the same shape as the four marked PALT-M6 cells.
